sources.title: Current team: founder and director Beatrice Fihn
sources.findings: Read Lex International current team page: Fihn is founder and director, former ICAN executive director and UNIDIR senior fellow. Other advisers and staff have their own responsibilities; do not attribute every Lex project or paper exclusively to Fihn.

sources.publisher: United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research
sources.title: Current people directory: Beatrice Fihn, Senior Fellow, Weapons of Mass Destruction
sources.findings: Read UNIDIR’s current people directory, specifically the Senior Fellows section: Beatrice Fihn is listed under Weapons of Mass Destruction. This corroborates the present fellowship, not a UN staff director post, diplomatic appointment or a new university degree.

sources.title: Historical speaker biography: leadership since 2014, prior work and university qualifications
sources.findings: Read ICAN NuclearBan Week 2022 historical speaker biography. It confirms leadership since 2014, prior WILPF/Reaching Critical Will work, an international-relations bachelor’s from Stockholm University and a law master’s from University College London. The old current-role wording is not reused as current. Graduation years were not independently established; University College London is kept distinct from the looser University of London wording elsewhere.

sources.publisher: International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons
sources.title: 22 November 2022: planned departure at the end of January 2023
sources.findings: Read ICAN’s 22 November 2022 announcement of departure at the end of January 2023. Announcement and effective departure are distinct. Its nine-years wording is not used to back-calculate an exact 2013 start against the historical biography’s explicit 2014.

sources.publisher: International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons
sources.title: 10 August 2023: Melissa Parke appointment and 1 September start
sources.findings: Read ICAN’s 10 August 2023 appointment announcement for Melissa Parke, specifying a 1 September start and saying Fihn had already left earlier that year. Do not imply Parke took office on Fihn’s last day or that the announcement itself was her start date.

sources.publisher: International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons
sources.title: 2017 Nobel Peace Prize: organisational recipient and joint 10 December lecture
sources.findings: Read ICAN Nobel page: the organisational laureate received the prize on 10 December 2017 and the Nobel Lecture was jointly delivered by Fihn and Setsuko Thurlow. Neither is entered as a separate individual laureate. The Nobel Foundation’s indexed 2017 ceremony address independently names ICAN as the award recipient; its direct page and individual prize pages returned 403.

sources.title: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons: adoption, signature and entry into force
sources.findings: Read UN Treaty Collection status entry and adoption note. Treaty adopted 7 July 2017, opened for signature 20 September 2017 and entered into force 22 January 2021 under article 15. Depositary registration date is not a new adoption date. Signature and party status are different columns; no unsupported claim of universal adherence or elimination is made. Current signatory/party counts are deliberately not frozen into this biographical text.

sources.publisher: International Committee of the Red Cross
sources.title: 18 January 2021: legal factsheet on the nuclear weapons prohibition treaty
sources.findings: Read ICRC legal factsheet dated 18 January 2021: treaty comprehensively prohibits nuclear weapons, addresses humanitarian consequences and complements existing nuclear agreements. Adoption, opening for signature, fiftieth ratification and entry into force are distinct. Legal prohibition is not proof that nuclear arsenals have disappeared; the page’s historical future tense is not treated as a future 2026 event.

sources.title: Summit Talks: founder role since 2023 and 2026 programme release months
sources.findings: Read Lex Summit Talks series and host sections, plus release listings: founder/director since 2023; Erik Tollefsen episode March 2026, Luis Vayas-Valdivieso April and Filippa Lentzos May. These are release months, not verified recording dates. The programme is hosted by Fihn, with each guest’s own expertise retained. The promotional personal Nobel-laureate wording is corrected to organisation representative.

sources.title: Fiscal sponsorship and hosted donor collaboratives: Lex International fund
sources.findings: Read Swiss Philanthropy Foundation’s hosted-funds section specifically for Lex International. It confirms a philanthropic fund hosted by the foundation, working with multiple sectors to strengthen international law. Other funds’ founding dates, donors and grant totals do not belong to Lex. Goals and claimed communications effects are not independently verified outcomes.

sources.title: 16 November 2026: Trenchers — Pin Drop production credits
sources.findings: Read Little Black Book’s Trenchers — Pin Drop work page, dated 16 November 2026. Fihn is one of several executive producers; Trevor McMahan is director and co-writer with Blaine Kneece. Publication is not filming or attendance. A related substantive indexed release report describes a five-part series scheduled 16–20 November; at the 18 November cutoff, later scheduled releases are not claimed complete. No film viewing or AI-system performance validation is claimed.

sources.title: 3 April 2018: school visit and explicit 1982 birth year
sources.findings: Read Mitt i Göteborg report of a return to Vättleskolan, dated 3 April 2018, including the explicit fact box giving birth year 1982. Exact 17 November birthday was found only in encyclopaedic/derivative material and was not independently corroborated, so precision remains year only. Loose Nobel wording and its 2006 campaign-founding claim are not adopted; childhood location is not assumed to establish exact birthplace.

sources.title: 18 November 2021: international-relations studies and WILPF internship
sources.findings: Read Stockholm University alumni interview dated 18 November 2021. It confirms international-relations studies and a WILPF internship that introduced her to nuclear disarmament. The university headline and captions simplify Nobel attribution; the organisational recipient is retained from prize records. No graduation year, legal professional registration or honorary academic degree is inferred.

sources.title: 31 January 2023: contemporary account confirming departure date
sources.findings: Read Susi Snyder’s contemporary ICAN account published 31 January 2023 on Humanitarian Disarmament: explicit departure on January 31. It corroborates the announced month and later successor announcement. Its first-women-ever Nobel claim and broad assertions of campaign effectiveness are not adopted as independently verified facts.
